findings.title: Monitor context drops schedule_type display conversion
findings.body: get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with get_schedule_type_display() on that copy. The returned context ignores the copy and sends monitor_environment.monitor.config instead. Occurrence events therefore keep the raw schedule_type (typically an integer enum) rather than the display string, and the conversion is dead code. Anything reading the monitor context (issue UI, consumers of the Kafka occurrence) will see the wrong schedule type.

findings.title: Failure-reason text does not match intended wording
findings.body: get_failure_reason builds each clause as "%(count)d %(status)s" (for example "2 missed") and then appends a single "check-ins detected". For more than one status that yields strings like "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected", not the documented "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". That string is stored as the important "Failure reason" evidence on the incident occurrence, so users see grammatically wrong, ambiguous failure summaries whenever the threshold window mixes statuses or the count is not the singular special case.
